Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5, branch lazy). Uncommitted changes: run
"git diff" there. New feature: option arith-liastar-main-solver moves the lazy LIA* cell
enumeration from a per-lambda subsolver into the MAIN solver. Design (see MainEnum in
src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h and mainSolverCheckStar/advanceStage/
emitDriverLemma/getModelDisjunct/getMainEnum/addEnumLemma in liastar_extension.cpp):
- lambda bound vars -> fresh integer skolems y; base(y) = predicate (ites/nots removed) + y>=0.
- Stage guards: h_0 => base(y); per discovered cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with
  h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k(y)); en.guard is the current h_k; each h is
  ensureLiteral'd and preferPhase'd true. h_0 additionally gets a split lemma.
- Driver lemma per (literal, stage): literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k), unguarded,
  where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal] (under-approximation built by processDisjunct)
  and p[v] is the vector predicate. Claimed satisfiability-preserving.
- Each full-effort round: catch up stages for cones discovered via other literals; if
  guard fixed false at level 0 (Valuation::isFixed) -> emit exact equivalence
  (processDisjunct complete=true); if guard true in SAT assignment -> read the cell from
  arithModel via getModelDisjunct (substitute+rewrite each atom of base; equality atoms
  false in model become strict inequalities; skolems missing from arithModel fall back to
  TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue), dedupe against d_lazyCones, advanceStage, then
  processDisjunct(false) emits the guarded equivalence g_k => (literal = star_k) and
  deactivates the previous g; then emitDriverLemma for the new stage.
- Tests: all 9 regress1/arith/liastar tests pass in this mode (Debug), and in the other
  three modes (accumulate/push-pop/eager); unit test passes.
Focus ONLY on problems introduced by the new main-solver mode (not pre-existing issues in
the subsolver paths). Report findings with concrete code references.
Lens: termination and progress. Questions to attack:
1. Can the procedure livelock: rounds where guard is false-but-not-fixed and the driver for the
   current stage was already emitted -- emitDriverLemma returns without queueing anything and
   doPendingLemmas sends nothing. Is there a scenario where the solver then answers sat with an
   unjustified positively-asserted literal, or loops forever without progress?
2. Duplicate-cell handling: when the model re-exhibits a known cell, the round emits at most a
   driver. Can this repeat indefinitely (same cell each round)? Note the stage that negates the
   cell was opened in the round that first harvested it -- is en.negated maintained consistently
   with d_lazyCones in ALL paths (addCone drops empty cones!)?
3. advanceStage in the catch-up loop vs processDisjunct ordering: en.negated = pairs.size() is
   executed twice in the harvest path (before/after processDisjunct). Off-by-one risks?
4. incremental mode (push/pop of the main solver between check-sats): lemmas/d_mainEnums/
   d_lastDriver are non-context state; what breaks (e.g. simple.smt2 has two check-sats)?

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

2	 * Top contributors (to current version):

10	 * directory for licensing information.
11	 * ****************************************************************************
12	 *
13	 * Extension to the theory of arithmetic handling the lia* (LIA star) operator.
14	 */
15	
16	#ifdef CVC5_USE_NORMALIZ
17	
18	#ifndef CVC5__THEORY__ARITH__LIASTAR_EXTENSION_H
19	#define CVC5__THEORY__ARITH__LIASTAR_EXTENSION_H
20	
21	#include <map>
22	#include <memory>
23	#include <vector>
24	
25	#include "expr/node.h"
26	#include "libnormaliz/libnormaliz.h"
27	#include "smt/env_obj.h"
28	#include "smt/solver_engine.h"
29	#include "theory/arith/liastar/liastar_proof_generator.h"
30	#include "theory/ext_theory.h"
31	#include "theory/theory.h"
32	
33	namespace cvc5::internal {
34	namespace theory {
35	namespace arith {
36	
37	class InferenceManager;
38	class TheoryArith;
39	
40	namespace liastar {
41	
42	/** Arbitrary-precision integers (the integer type handed to Normaliz). */
43	typedef mpz_class Integer;
44	/** A row of arithmetic terms, e.g. the monomials of one cone contribution. */
45	typedef std::vector<Node> Vector;
46	
47	/**
48	 * Extension to TheoryArith deciding the lia* operator STAR_CONTAINS.
49	 *
50	 * A literal
51	 *     (int.star-contains (lambda ((x_1 Int) ... (x_n Int)) p) v_1 ... v_n)
52	 * asserts that the vector v = (v_1, ..., v_n) belongs to the additive closure
53	 * (the *star*) of the set S = { x in Z^n : p(x), x >= 0 }, i.e. that v is a
54	 * finite sum of vectors each satisfying p. The extension decides such literals
55	 * by reducing them to plain linear integer arithmetic, following
56	 *
57	 * - Levatich, M., Bjorner, N., Piskac, R., Shoham, S. (2020).
58	 *   Solving LIA* Using Approximations.
59	 *   VMCAI 2020.
60	 *   https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-39322-9_17
61	 *
62	 * The reduction views each convex cell (DNF disjunct) of p as a polyhedral
63	 * cone, computes the cone's Hilbert basis and module generators with Normaliz,
64	 * and encodes the star of the union of cells as a system of linear constraints
65	 * over fresh non-negative multipliers (the "star constraints"). The reduction
66	 * lemma `literal = star` is sent through TheoryArith's inference manager. See
67	 * the file comment of liastar_extension.cpp for the full picture.
68	 *
69	 * The main entry point is checkFullEffort(...), called by TheoryArith at
70	 * full/last-call effort with the current candidate arithmetic model. Two
71	 * strategies are available (option arith-lia-star-lazy):
72	 * - eager (`eagerCheckStar`): normalize p to DNF and reduce in one shot;
73	 * - lazy (`lazyCheckStar`): discover one convex cell per refinement round from
74	 *   models of a persistent incremental subsolver, asserting guarded
75	 *   under-approximations until every cell is covered.
76	 */
77	class LiaStarExtension : EnvObj
78	{
79	 public:
80	  LiaStarExtension(Env& env, TheoryArith& containing);
81	  ~LiaStarExtension();
82	
83	  /**
84	   * Does non-context dependent setup for a node connected to a theory:
85	   * registers STAR_CONTAINS terms with the extended theory and records that
86	   * this extension has work to do.
87	   */
88	  void preRegisterTerm(TNode n);
89	
90	  /**
91	   * Performs the main checks for liastar arithmetic, based on the current
92	   * (linear) arithmetic model from `arithModel`. This method may already send
93	   * lemmas, but most lemmas are buffered and sent at LAST_CALL effort by
94	   * TheoryArith. The motivation for this strategy is to allow other
95	   * non-terminating theories (e.g. quantifiers, strings) to run full effort
96	   * checks, before sending the lemmas generated by liastar.
97	   *
98	   * For each STAR_CONTAINS assertion this emits a non-negativity lemma and a
99	   * split on the substituted predicate p[v], and then -- unless the current
100	   * model already satisfies the literal -- reduces the literal via the eager
101	   * or lazy strategy.
102	   *
103	   * @param arithModel a map of the form { v1 -> c1, ..., vn -> cn } which
104	   *   represents the linear arithmetic theory solver's contribution to the
105	   *   current candidate model, where v1, ..., vn are arithmetic variables and
106	   *   c1, ..., cn are constants
107	   * @param termSet the set of terms relevant in the current check
108	   */
109	  void checkFullEffort(std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel,
110	                       const std::set<Node>& termSet);
111	
112	  /** Does this class need a call to check(...) at last call effort? */
113	  bool hasLiaStarTerms() const { return d_hasLiaStarTerms; }
114	
115	 private:
116	  /**
117	   * Collect from TheoryArith's fact queue the STAR_CONTAINS atoms asserted in
118	   * the current context. Both polarities are reduced to the positive atom:
119	   * the reduction lemma `atom = star` handles either polarity (the
120	   * surrounding SAT solver applies the negation).
121	   */
122	  void getAssertions(std::vector<Node>& assertions);
123	
124	  /**
125	   * Normalize the body p of the lambda `n` into DNF and render each disjunct
126	   * as a Normaliz constraint matrix (see `LiaStarUtils::getMatrices`).
127	   *
128	   * @param n a lambda (lambda ((x_1 Int) ... (x_n Int)) p) with p in QF_LIA
129	   * @return one (constraint rows, disjunct node) pair per DNF disjunct of p,
130	   *   i.e. one per cone
131	   */
132	  const std::vector<std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>>
133	  convertQFLIAToMatrices(Node n);
134	
135	  /**
136	   * Eager path: build a Normaliz cone for every DNF disjunct of the predicate
137	   * and accumulate the star constraints over all of them. Empty (infeasible)
138	   * cones are skipped.
139	   *
140	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal; its children after the lambda are the
141	   *   vector v
142	   * @param pairs one (constraint rows, disjunct node) pair per disjunct, as
143	   *   returned by `convertQFLIAToMatrices`
144	   * @return the non-empty cones, each paired with the disjunct it came from
145	   *   (used by `getMembershipDisjuncts` for the debug trace), and the star
146	   *   constraints: fresh multiplier skolems with their side constraints plus
147	   *   the sum constraints tying v to the cones' contributions. Their
148	   *   conjunction is equivalent to `v in S*`.
149	   */
150	  std::pair<std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>,
151	            std::vector<Node>>
152	  getCones(Node n,
153	           const std::vector<std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>>& pairs);
154	
155	  /**
156	   * Lazy path: build the cone for a single disjunct and append it to the list
157	   * of cones for `n[0]` (the lambda) stored in `d_lazyCones`. If the cone is
158	   * empty (the disjunct is infeasible) it is not added.
159	   *
160	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal
161	   * @param pair the disjunct's constraint rows and node, as returned by
162	   *   `LiaStarUtils::getMatrix`
163	   */
164	  void addCone(Node n, const std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>& pair);
165	
166	  /**
167	   * Lazy path: return the star constraints over all cones accumulated so far
168	   * in `d_lazyCones[n[0]]` (the cones added by previous calls to `addCone`).
169	   *
170	   * The per-cone constraints (and their fresh skolems) are computed only for
171	   * cones that have not been processed in a previous call and are accumulated
172	   * in `d_starConstraints[n[0]]`, so the skolems stay stable across refinement
173	   * rounds; the sum constraints, which span all cones, are rebuilt from the
174	   * accumulated `d_lambdas[n[0]]` on each call.
175	   */
176	  std::vector<Node> getStarConstraints(Node n);
177	
178	  /**
179	   * Debug helper, used only for the "liastar-ext-smt" trace. Builds the
180	   * *membership* encoding `v in S`: one existentially quantified formula per
181	   * (cone, module generator) stating that v is the single element
182	   * `g + sum_j l_j h_j` of that cone. The disjunction of all returned
183	   * formulas is equivalent to the predicate itself, which the emitted trace
184	   * queries let an external solver verify.
185	   *
186	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal
187	   * @param cones the cones with their originating disjuncts, as returned by
188	   *   `getCones`
189	   * @return each membership formula paired with the disjunct it encodes
190	   */
191	  std::vector<std::pair<Node, Node>> getMembershipDisjuncts(
192	      Node n, std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>& cones);
193	
194	  /**
195	   * Performs the eager Hilbert-basis reduction for a single STAR_CONTAINS
196	   * literal. Generates the star reduction lemma equating `literal` with the
197	   * conjunction of star constraints derived from the cones of `lambda`
198	   * (== literal[0]), and sends it via the inference manager. Does nothing if
199	   * the literal has already been processed.
200	   */
201	  void eagerCheckStar(Node literal, Node lambda);
202	
203	  /**
204	   * Performs one round of the lazy Hilbert-basis reduction for a single
205	   * STAR_CONTAINS literal: refines the literal's subsolver with the negations
206	   * of the cone-disjuncts discovered since the previous round, then delegates
207	   * to `lazyHilbert`. Does nothing if the literal has been fully reduced.
208	   */
209	  void lazyCheckStar(Node literal, Node lambda);
210	
211	  /**
212	   * A persistent, incremental subsolver dedicated to one lambda (one
213	   * STAR_CONTAINS predicate). It is used to enumerate the convex cells of the
214	   * predicate's satisfying region: it is seeded once with the (nonnegative)
215	   * predicate at the base user level and then refined across rounds with the
216	   * negations of the discovered cone-disjuncts, either one assertion per
217	   * disjunct (the default) or as a single cumulative refined formula under
218	   * push/pop (option arith-liastar-push-pop); see `lazyCheckStar`.
219	   */
220	  struct Subsolver
221	  {
222	    /** the incremental QF_LIA subsolver. */
223	    std::unique_ptr<SolverEngine> engine;
224	    /** the lambda's bound variables ... */
225	    std::vector<Node> from;
226	    /** ... and the fresh skolem constants substituted for them, since a
227	     * subsolver cannot be given a formula with free (bound) variables. */
228	    std::vector<Node> to;
229	    /**
230	     * The (nonnegative) predicate in skolem space. It is already asserted in
231	     * `engine` at the base user level (so it survives every pop); it is kept
232	     * only to read off the predicate's atoms when building a disjunct from
233	     * the model.
234	     */
235	    Node base;
236	    /**
237	     * Push/pop strategy only: the union (disjunction), in skolem space, of
238	     * the cone-disjuncts discovered so far. Its negation is the refined
239	     * formula currently asserted in `engine`.
240	     */
241	    Node covered;
242	    /** Push/pop strategy only: whether a refined formula is currently
243	     * asserted, i.e. whether `engine` has a pushed frame to pop before
244	     * asserting the next refined formula. */
245	    bool pushed = false;
246	    /** number of cones in `d_lazyCones[lambda]` already negated in `engine`
247	     * (or, for the push/pop strategy, folded into `covered`). */
248	    size_t negated = 0;
249	  };
250	
251	  /**
252	   * Returns the subsolver for `lambda`, creating and seeding it (with the
253	   * nonnegative predicate) on first use.
254	   */
255	  Subsolver& getSubsolver(Node lambda);
256	
257	  /**
258	   * One lazy refinement round for `literal`: ask the subsolver for a model in
259	   * a region of the predicate not yet covered by a cone, read off the convex
260	   * cell containing it (`LiaStarUtils::getDisjunct`), and hand it to
261	   * `processDisjunct`.
262	   */
263	  void lazyHilbert(Node literal, Subsolver& sub);
264	
265	  /**
266	   * Shared tail of one lazy refinement round (used by both the subsolver and
267	   * the main-solver enumeration): turn `disjunct` -- a freshly discovered
268	   * cell of the predicate, in bound-variable space -- into a cone, rebuild
269	   * the star constraints over all cones found so far, and emit the reduction
270	   * lemma: guarded by a fresh boolean while the star is still an
271	   * under-approximation (`complete` false), unconditional once every cell is
272	   * covered (`complete` true, `disjunct` is then the false constraint).
273	   */
274	  void processDisjunct(Node literal, Node disjunct, bool complete);
275	
276	  /**
277	   * State for enumerating the convex cells of one lambda's predicate in the
278	   * main solver (option arith-liastar-main-solver), replacing the dedicated
279	   * subsolver. The lambda's bound variables are replaced by fresh skolems
280	   * (`from` -> `to`) that live in the main solver, constrained through a
281	   * chain of stage guards: h_0 => base, and for every discovered
282	   * cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k)
283	   * (two constant-size lemmas per stage, accumulate style). The current
284	   * stage guard h_k therefore activates `base and not(D_1) ... and not(D_k)`,
285	   * i.e. it places the skolems in a cell not yet covered by a cone; the cell
286	   * is then read off the main solver's candidate arithmetic model.
287	   *
288	   * The enumeration is driven by the literal itself: each stage emits the
289	   * (satisfiability-preserving) driver lemma
290	   *     literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k),
291	   * so a model that claims the literal without certifying it must activate
292	   * h_k and thereby exhibit a fresh cell; once every cell is covered the h_k
293	   * branch closes by conflict and the driver leaves exactly the certified
294	   * branches. Completeness is additionally detected when the SAT solver
295	   * fixes the stage guard false at level 0 (`Valuation::isFixed`), at which
296	   * point the exact reduction is emitted.
297	   */
298	  struct MainEnum
299	  {
300	    /** the lambda's bound variables ... */
301	    std::vector<Node> from;
302	    /** ... and the fresh skolems substituted for them in the main solver. */
303	    std::vector<Node> to;
304	    /** The (nonnegative) predicate in skolem space. It is asserted under the
305	     * first stage guard; it is also used to read off the predicate's atoms
306	     * when building a disjunct from the model. */
307	    Node base;
308	    /** The current stage guard h_k (a decision variable, biased true). */
309	    Node guard;
310	    /** number of cones in `d_lazyCones[lambda]` already negated via stage
311	     * guards. */
312	    size_t negated = 0;
313	  };
314	
315	  /**
316	   * Returns the main-solver enumeration state for `lambda`, creating it (and
317	   * queueing its seed lemmas: the guard split and `guard => base`) on first
318	   * use.
319	   */
320	  MainEnum& getMainEnum(Node lambda);
321	
322	  /**
323	   * One refinement round of the main-solver lazy strategy for `literal`:
324	   * depending on the guard's value in the current SAT assignment, read a
325	   * fresh cell from the candidate model (guard true), conclude completeness
326	   * (guard fixed false), or bias the guard and wait (otherwise). See
327	   * `MainEnum`.
328	   */
329	  void mainSolverCheckStar(Node literal,
330	                           Node lambda,
331	                           const std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel);
332	
333	  /**
334	   * Read the cell of `en.base` containing the current candidate arithmetic
335	   * model: fix the truth value of every atom of `en.base` under `arithModel`
336	   * (consulting `TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue` for skolems missing
337	   * from the map) and return the conjunction in bound-variable space.
338	   * Returns the null node if some atom cannot be evaluated to a constant.
339	   */
340	  Node getModelDisjunct(MainEnum& en, const std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel);
341	
342	  /**
343	   * Queue a main-solver enumeration lemma (InferenceId ARITH_LIA_STAR_ENUM),
344	   * skipping lemmas that rewrite to a constant.
345	   */
346	  void addEnumLemma(Node lemma);
347	
348	  /**
349	   * Open a new enumeration stage for `en`: a fresh guard that activates the
350	   * previous stage's constraints plus the negation of the newly covered
351	   * cell `skolemDisjunct` (in skolem space).
352	   */
353	  void advanceStage(MainEnum& en, Node skolemDisjunct);
354	
355	  /**
356	   * Emit, once per (literal, stage), the driver lemma
357	   * `literal => (p[v] or star or guard)`; see `MainEnum`.
358	   */
359	  void emitDriverLemma(Node literal, MainEnum& en);
360	
361	  /** node manager */
362	  NodeManager* d_nm;
363	  /** commonly used terms */
364	  Node d_true;
365	  Node d_false;
366	  Node d_zero;
367	  Node d_one;
368	  /** The theory of arithmetic containing this extension. */
369	  TheoryArith& d_arith;

content.text: I have completed the analysis. Let me verify a couple of line references before writing up the findings.

findings.title: Incremental push/pop desynchronizes MainEnum/d_lastDriver from the SAT solver: enumeration runs with unconstrained guards and skolems, poisoning d_lazyCones permanently
findings.detail: All main-solver enumeration lemmas (guard split, h_0 => base at src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:874-883, chain/negation lemmas in advanceStage:994-1006, drivers:1008-1036, guarded equivalences from processDisjunct) are ordinary theory lemmas: minisat pins them at the assertion level where they were sent and Solver::pop() deletes them (src/prop/minisat/core/Solver.cc:1972-1973). The CnfStream node-to-literal map is also user-context (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:86-90, cnf_stream.cpp:41-42). But the bookkeeping that decides whether to (re)send them is plain non-context state: d_mainEnums (en.guard, en.negated), d_lastDriver, d_lazyCones (liastar_extension.h:449-462). After a `(pop 1)` (exactly the structure of test/regress/cli/regress1/arith/liastar/simple.smt2, which has two `(push) assert check-sat (pop)` blocks over the SAME lambda), the next check-sat finds: (a) getMainEnum early-returns (liastar_extension.cpp:828-832), so h_0 => base is never re-sent; (b) the catch-up loop sees en.negated == d_lazyCones.size() (1060-1070), so no stage negation is re-sent; (c) for a re-asserted identical literal, emitDriverLemma's memo d_lastDriver[literal]==en.guard (1021-1024) suppresses the driver too, making EVERY round silent -> the solver answers sat with the star literal completely unconstrained (unjustified sat, or wrong-sat on an unsat re-query). For a different literal over the same lambda (simple.smt2's case), the driver IS sent, re-Tseitin-ing the stale guard as a brand-new, otherwise UNCONSTRAINED Boolean (its freezePolarity bias is also gone): the SAT solver can set it true, mainSolverCheckStar then reaches getModelDisjunct (1109) with skolems en.to no longer tied to base, so the 'cell' read off the model need not satisfy the predicate at all (getModelDisjunct never checks that base evaluates true under the model, 898-992). processDisjunct then adds a cone for a region possibly OUTSIDE p to the non-context d_lazyCones[lambda], making every later star an over-approximation of S* -> unsound sat in this and all later check-sats. simple.smt2 currently passes only by luck: p[4,4] rewrites to constant true so the model-value shortcut answers before any of this is exercised. Fix direction: make d_mainEnums/d_lastDriver user-context-dependent (or re-seed and re-emit all stage lemmas when the cached guard is no longer a SAT literal / when entering a new user context), and have getModelDisjunct verify the model actually satisfies en.base before harvesting.

findings.title: Completeness detection via Valuation::isFixed never fires when the star assertion is under a user push or check-sat-assuming
findings.detail: mainSolverCheckStar concludes 'every cell covered' only via `assigned && !guardValue && val.isFixed(en.guard)` (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1086-1094). PropEngine::isFixed delegates to MinisatSatSolver::isFixed, which requires `intro_level(var)==0 && user_level(var)==0 && level(var)==0` (src/prop/minisat/minisat.cpp:290-294). The stage guards are created by ensureLiteral DURING solving, so their intro_level equals minisat's current assertionLevel, which is >= 1 whenever the query sits under `(push)` or check-sat-assuming (ContextManager::internalPush -> PropEngine::push, src/smt/context_manager.cpp:142-154; only assumptions/user pushes bump it). Hence in exactly those incremental scenarios (including simple.smt2, the only incremental regression), isFixed(en.guard) is ALWAYS false even after not-h_k is propagated at decision level 0, and the complete=true branch is dead code: processDisjunct(literal, false, true) is never called, the exact equivalence `literal = star` is never emitted, and the literal is never added to d_processedStarTerms. Consequences: the enumeration's documented termination mechanism never triggers under push; refutation/sat answers must instead emerge indirectly from driver-clause conflicts (which happens to work for concrete vectors, which is why simple.smt2's first check still answers unsat), the literal keeps being re-processed every full-effort round forever, and any case that genuinely needs the exact equivalence (notably justifying a negated literal) silently degrades. The guard-false-but-not-fixed state the design treats as transient ('wait and re-emit driver', 1096-1105) becomes the permanent state after coverage completes.

findings.title: No progress or justification mechanism for negatively asserted star literals; silent rounds let the solver answer sat with the enumeration incomplete
findings.detail: Q1 verdict: for POSITIVELY asserted literals, within a single check-sat the silent rounds are safe: the driver clause `literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k)` (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1008-1036) persists in the SAT solver (theory lemmas are non-removable), and emitDriverLemma is re-keyed on en.guard at each stage advance, so any accepted full assignment with h_k false must Boolean-satisfy p[v] or star_k, which the consistent arithmetic model then genuinely certifies (star_k is an under-approximation, so the sat answer is justified); a silent full-effort round simply ends the search with sat, so no livelock. But getAssertions reduces both polarities to the positive atom (liastar_extension.cpp:304-308) while the driver lemma is vacuous when the atom is asserted FALSE. For `(not (star-contains ...))` nothing forces the stage guards: preferPhase/freezePolarity is only a decision bias, and not-h_k can be propagated at a non-zero level (e.g. the y-atoms get decided into an already-covered cell via phase saving, falsifying the Tseitin of not-D_i, which propagates not-h_i and, through the chain h_k => h_{k-1}, all later guards). In that state mainSolverCheckStar takes the `!assigned || !guardValue` branch (1096-1105), emitDriverLemma is a no-op for the already-emitted stage, doPendingLemmas sends nothing (nonneg/split are cached in d_lemmasSent), the theory contributes nothing, and the solver finalizes sat with the negated literal never semantically checked (the extension never calls setModelUnsound; grep over src/theory/arith/liastar/ confirms). The old subsolver mode structurally cannot accept a model this way: lazyCheckStar/lazyHilbert emits fresh-guard lemmas on EVERY round until the enumeration is provably complete, so every uncompleted round sends a lemma and the search cannot stop early. (Caveat on scope: justifying negative polarity via the free-skolem equivalence is weak in the pre-existing modes too, but accepting a model with the enumeration incomplete and zero lemmas emitted is introduced by the main-solver mode.) Minimal fix: call d_im.setModelUnsound(...) on any silent round in which an asserted star literal is not certified by the model, and/or emit a driver for the negative polarity (e.g. not(literal) => (not p[v]) ... or guard) so the enumeration is also driven by refutation obligations.

findings.title: Duplicate-cell check compares the raw model disjunct against normalized stored disjuncts, and empty-cone cells have no record at all
findings.detail: Q2 verdict. The dedupe loop in mainSolverCheckStar (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1119-1128) compares the RAW getModelDisjunct output -- which renders false non-equality atoms as `atom.notNode()` (965-968) -- against d_lazyCones entries, which store the node returned by LiaStarUtils::getMatrix AFTER processDisjunct has run removeItesAndNots (1183-1197; getMatrix returns its input node, liastar_utils.cpp:883+; removeItesAndNots rewrites negated comparisons into positive ones, liastar_utils.cpp:123-136). So any cell containing a negated atom can never match: the check is structurally ineffective in the very scenarios it exists for. Additionally, addCone silently drops empty (integer-infeasible) cones (650-671), so a cell that WAS harvested and negated by a stage has no representative in d_lazyCones either. Within a single check-sat this is fully masked -- once the stage lemma h_{k+1} => not(D)(y) is sent (same round, doPendingLemmas), any later model with the current guard true must falsify some atom of D, so re-exhibiting a known raw disjunct is impossible and the dedupe branch is effectively dead code; each guard-true round harvests a semantically new cell and the enumeration terminates (finitely many atom-truth-assignments). The danger is in the stale-state scenarios of the incremental finding: with stage lemmas popped but d_lazyCones retained, known cells ARE re-exhibited, the broken comparison fails to catch most of them (unbounded duplicate cones, duplicated star skolems/constraints), and when it DOES catch one the round is completely silent (driver already emitted for the current stage) -> unjustified sat. Fix: store and compare the same normal form (e.g. dedupe on the post-removeItesAndNots node), and keep a record (separate from d_lazyCones) of every stage-negated cell including ones whose cones were dropped as empty.

findings.title: Double 'en.negated = pairs.size()' in the harvest path: currently consistent (no off-by-one), but the invariant is implicit and fragile
findings.detail: Q3 verdict. The assignment appears at src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1070 (after the catch-up loop) and again at 1143 (after advanceStage + processDisjunct). Tracing the harvest path: at 1070 en.negated == pairs.size() == k with stages negating exactly cones 0..k-1; advanceStage(1137) pre-negates the NEW cell; processDisjunct -> addCone appends at most one cone (the same cell, normalized), so at 1143 pairs.size() is k+1 (or k if the cone was empty and dropped) and en.negated = pairs.size() is correct in both cases -- the freshly appended cone is exactly the one the new stage already negated, and a dropped empty cone leaves the count unchanged. The complete=true path adds no cone (disjunct=false builds an empty cone) and correctly skips the update. Two literals sharing a lambda also stay consistent because every path that grows d_lazyCones[lambda] in this mode runs through this same function for some literal of that lambda and re-synchronizes before returning. So: no off-by-one today. However the correctness rests on three unstated invariants: (1) processDisjunct/addCone appends AT MOST ONE cone per call, (2) advanceStage was called for precisely that prospective cone beforehand, and (3) nothing else appends to d_lazyCones[lambda] between 1137 and 1143. Blanket-assigning pairs.size() (instead of incrementing per staged cone, or asserting Assert(pairs.size() <= en.negated + 1)) would silently mark cones as negated-without-a-stage if any of these change -- which would let an uncovered cone's region keep re-appearing in models with the guard true, i.e. a genuine livelock. Recommend replacing the second assignment with an increment guarded by whether addCone actually appended, plus an assertion tying en.negated to pairs.size().

findings.title: Unguarded driver lemmas share per-lambda multiplier skolems across literals (pre-existing root, surfaced by the new drivers)
findings.detail: emitDriverLemma asserts d_lastStarLia[literal] unguarded (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1034). The star formulas for different literals over the SAME lambda share the multiplier skolems mu/l, because getStarConstraints caches per-cone constraints and (point, rays) contributions keyed by lambda (d_starConstraints/d_lambdas, liastar_extension.cpp:673-731) while building per-literal sum constraints `v_i = Sigma contributions(mu)` over the SAME skolems. Once coverage completes and the guards are forced false, two positively asserted literals with different vectors v1 != v2 that both need the star branch make their drivers jointly require v1 = Sigma(mu) and v2 = Sigma'(mu) over shared mu, which over-constrains (independent witnesses are intended) and can produce a spurious UNSAT on a satisfiable instance. The root cause (per-lambda skolem sharing) is pre-existing -- the subsolver path's complete equivalences literal = star have the same defect -- so this is flagged for awareness rather than as a regression: the new mode adds more unguarded, never-retractable occurrences of these shared-skolem formulas (one driver per literal per stage) where the subsolver path only exposes unguarded occurrences at completion. Per-literal (not per-lambda) multiplier skolems, or existential closure of the star body, would remove the coupling.

content.content: Structured output provided successfully

content.text: Analysis complete. Findings delivered via structured output: one critical (incremental push/pop staleness of `d_mainEnums`/`d_lastDriver` vs popped lemmas, permitting unconstrained-skolem harvesting that permanently poisons `d_lazyCones`), two major (the `Valuation::isFixed` completeness check is dead under user pushes since stage guards have `intro_level >= 1`; negative-polarity literals have no driver/progress mechanism and silent rounds can yield unjustified sat with no `setModelUnsound` safety net), and three minor (raw-vs-normalized dedupe mismatch plus untracked empty-cone cells; the double `en.negated = pairs.size()` is consistent today but rests on implicit invariants; shared per-lambda multiplier skolems in unguarded drivers, with a pre-existing root).
